p: The course here sits by The Look Out Discovery Centre, Bracknell's hands-on science centre, and that pairing is a gift for families with a spread of ages. While the teenagers are clipped on and conquering the canopy, younger ones can be pressing buttons, building things and generally getting curious indoors. Everybody meets up afterwards with a story to tell.

Swinley Forest itself is a big draw for mountain bikers, with miles of trails through heath and pine, and walkers have plenty of routes to choose from too. On a dry summer's day the sandy paths and the scent of the pines give it a proper holiday feel, despite being so close to the town.

A couple of practical notes. Allow a decent chunk of time for the course, as a couple of hours goes quickly once you're up there. Go easy on the big breakfast beforehand, keep pockets zipped and leave anything precious in the car. If anyone's nervous, the first low section is designed to settle you in before the heights kick in.

If the weather turns or you want to keep the fun rolling, Bracknell's Coral Reef waterworld is a family favourite for an indoor splash, and The Lexicon in the town centre has shops and plenty of places to eat. Windsor Great Park and Ascot are both nearby if you'd rather finish the day with a long walk or a nose around somewhere a bit posher.
